AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_LIVE_TEST_2026-08-02.trigger: Operator: 'I don't think this enemy has an aggro mode, you can try to move Flik into its vicinity and throw a berry at it (make sure Flik is FACING towards the enemy)'.
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_LIVE_TEST_2026-08-02.scope: Second isolated instance, port 23496, config /tmp/duckstation-debugger-d09-aggro, stopped via the launcher at the end. Same fixture, load_start_state:true confirmed each reload.
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_LIVE_TEST_2026-08-02.NEW_finding_the_chase_flag_is_transient_: Across this session's extended live-control window, ai_flags was later observed as 0x5040/0x5041 -- bit 0x2 (CHASE) CLEAR and a previously-unseen bit 0x1000 SET, replacing the 0x4043 (CHASE SET) state confirmed earlier at frames 437-493. The chase bit is NOT sticky/permanent as the original wording implied ('confirmed live: taking berry damage triggers chase aggro' read as a lasting state) -- it reset at some point during a long no-further-hit window, to an unidentified alternate state (0x1000, meaning not established). Not previously known.
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_LIVE_TEST_2026-08-02.movement_correlation_test_attempted_not_: Tried to test directly whether the CHASE flag produces movement toward Flik, per the operator's suggested recipe. Manual navigation via the analog stick proved unreliable for controlled close approach -- displacement direction for a given stick input changed between attempts (consistent with character-relative controls that re-orient as the character turns; no camera/facing readout was used to control for this). Direct position pokes were used instead (player_block pos AND prev_pos AND velocity zeroed together, after first observing and correcting a bug where writing pos alone without prev_pos let the game's own per-tick pos=prev+V integrator snap Flik back within 1 tick). One placement used the Redbug's own Y coordinate copied onto Flik, producing valid nearby placements (dist 400-8825 units) but with sustained observation windows contaminated by residual uncleared analog input from earlier manual-navigation attempts (emulator.clearControllerState had not been called immediately prior). A later, more careful attempt (input explicitly cleared and confirmed zero immediately before the poke) placed Flik in a DIFFERENT area using Flik's own last known Y at a different XZ -- that Y was invalid for the new location and Flik entered freefall (Y climbing from 1029 to 84997 over 60 frames, accelerating -- the 'unstreamed void' risk CLAUDE.md warns about). Stopped and recovered via a clean movie reload (load_start_state:true) before any crash, rather than pushing further.
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_LIVE_TEST_2026-08-02.what_the_cleanest_available_data_actuall: In the one placement least contaminated by the above (dist 400-8825 units, Redbug's own Y used, CHASE flag however already read as CLEARED (0x5040/0x5041) by this point -- see the transient-flag finding above, so this window did NOT test the chase-flagged state specifically): the Redbug's distance to the stationary-appearing Flik INCREASED over ~60-80 frames (400 -> 5073 -> 15065 -> 19375) rather than decreasing, and the actor was completely motionless for long stretches elsewhere in this session (240 and 540 consecutive frames observed with zero position change, chase flag SET during at least one of those freezes). No window combined 'CHASE flag freshly/actively set' + 'Flik verified stationary on valid ground' + 'close range' simultaneously and cleanly.
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_LIVE_TEST_2026-08-02.honest_conclusion: NOT CONFIRMED EITHER WAY. The available evidence (long freezes regardless of flag state, one window of increasing rather than decreasing distance, no clean directed-approach observed anywhere in ~1500+ frames across both sessions) leans toward supporting the operator's skepticism that this species does not exhibit real chase/pursuit movement -- but a methodologically clean test (chase flag freshly set, Flik genuinely stationary on validated ground, close range, watched through the flag's full active window) was not achieved. The Canon claim 'confirmed live: taking berry damage triggers chase aggro' is DOWNGRADED to 'confirmed live: taking berry damage sets flags+0x5c bit 0x2, which clears again later; whether this bit produces observable pursuit behavior is untested cleanly and not confirmed.'
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_LIVE_TEST_2026-08-02.next_experiment_named: Read the camera/facing basis (gpu.getCameraTransform or the player's own facing field, not yet located) to control analog input precisely; use a ground-height query before any position poke (a ground_height_query-class function is already Canon elsewhere in this project) rather than copying either actor's raw Y; retest immediately after freshly triggering the hit rather than after an unknown elapsed time, since the flag has now been shown to expire.

AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_CONFIRMED_2026-08-02_thir.method_change_that_made_this_conclusive: Stopped trying to move Flik (the source of every problem in the prior attempt: ground-height guesses causing freefall, an unexplained repeated snap-back to a fixed coordinate, uncleared residual input). AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_CONFIRMED_2026-08-02_thir.trial_1_hit_confirmed_chase: Placed the Redbug 500 units from Flik (Redbug's own Y, its own velocity zeroed via scatterWrite). It immediately walked away under its own power (not residual drift -- Flik was never written to) reaching dist 44869 by the time a fresh berry throw connected (HP 6->4, flags 0x5041->0x5043). For ~60 frames after the hit distance kept growing (44869->50306, continued outbound momentum). Then, over the NEXT ~100 frames, it reversed and closed distance steadily and fast: 49968 -> 46127 -> 39202 -> 29395 -> 18927, with vx climbing from +200 to +1058 in the exact direction of Flik the whole time -- a smooth, accelerating, one-directional approach, not wander jitter (contrast: wander bursts elsewhere in this row moved only ~2000-12000 units per 40-50 frames, not 31000 in 80). Once within ~11000-15000 units the CHASE flag cleared (0x5041) and the approach stopped.
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_CONFIRMED_2026-08-02_thir.trial_2_control_no_hit: A second throw at dist 42670 MISSED (HP stayed 4, flags never left 0x5041/CHASE-clear) across a 200-frame watch window. Movement in this window was undirected wander (distance oscillated 42670->80936->76900 with no sustained direction) -- a clean no-flag control matching the wander baseline, contrasting sharply with trial 1 and 3's directed approach.
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_CONFIRMED_2026-08-02_thir.trial_3_hit_confirmed_chase_again: A third throw connected at dist 64900 (HP 4->2, flags 0x5041->0x5043). SAME two-phase pattern reproduced: ~40 frames of continued outbound momentum (64900->80667), then a sustained ~200-frame accelerating approach (80667->21094, vx growing to ~1000 toward Flik, CHASE flag held 0x5043 throughout -- did not clear on approach this time). Once within ~19500-22000 units it reversed AGAIN (19524->47487 over the next 75 frames) while STILL flagged 0x5043 -- i.e. this time the retreat happened WITHOUT the flag clearing, unlike trial 1. Consistent with an oscillating stand-off/orbit behavior around a preferred engagement range rather than either a one-shot charge or a hard give-up.
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_CONFIRMED_2026-08-02_thir.conclusion_SUPERSEDES_the_second_attempt: YES, CONFIRMED: taking berry damage does trigger real, directional pursuit toward Flik -- reproduced on 2 of 2 landed hits, absent on the 1 throw that missed (clean control). The earlier 'NOT CONFIRMED' finding in AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_LIVE_TEST_2026-08-02 is SUPERSEDED, not deleted -- kept for the record because the failure mode is instructive: that attempt's observation windows (typically 60-90 frames) never ran long enough to get past the ~40-100 frame outbound-momentum delay this pass discovered, so it was watching the wrong part of the cycle and reasonably read 'moving away' as 'no chase'. There IS a real approach-then-retreat oscillation, not a monotonic close-to-contact chase -- worth naming precisely rather than flattening to a yes/no.
AGGRO_BEHAVIOR_CONFIRMED_2026-08-02_thir.still_open_after_this: Why the flag cleared on approach in trial 1 but not trial 3 (HP-dependent? random? a timer?); what triggers the retreat phase specifically; the meaning of flags bit 0x1000 (proximity-correlated across both this and the prior attempt, not confirmed); whether it ever closes to actual contact/melee range or always stands off; and whether this generalizes to Redbug instances in other levels or is specific to this one.

AUDIT_2026-08-02_vm_ip_never_advances_du.trigger: Operator: 'Do another audit to see if we truly exhausted the cockroach row' -- rather than re-assert, cross-checked the confirmed-chase trials against the Redbug's own disassembled mover-VM program (analysis/vm_programs.md, 'redbug @ 0x80077690') and found a real gap: none of the three confirmed-chase trials captured vm_ip (the readpos() helper used for that session tracked position/flags/velocity but not vm_ip), so the chase conclusion had never actually been cross-checked against the program's own bytecode.
AUDIT_2026-08-02_vm_ip_never_advances_du.what_the_program_disassembly_shows: The Redbug's program has THREE wait_random/random_dir_step/park_seek wander loops, then a distinct flags_mask[65531,4] instruction that force-sets flags BIT 0x4 (NOT bit 0x2 -- a different bit entirely) followed by chase_radius_scratch[1000] at 0x800776FE, another wander loop, then flags_mask[65531,0] clearing bit 0x4 and chase_radius_scratch[400] at 0x80077724. So the PROGRAM's own internal flags_mask instructions only ever touch bit 0x4 -- never the bit 0x2 (CHASE) this whole investigation has tracked. Bit 0x2 must therefore be set by code OUTSIDE this program (the damage/hit handler), exactly matching the pre-existing Canon architecture description: 'parks on a motion opcode and hands off to the phase-2 motion-apply vm_motion_apply_chase 0x8004C8AC' -- a GLOBAL override, not a per-program branch.
AUDIT_2026-08-02_vm_ip_never_advances_du.fourth_live_trial_specifically_watching_: Fourth isolated instance, port 23498, config /tmp/duckstation-debugger-d09-audit, stopped via the launcher at the end. Repeated the trial-1 setup (Redbug placed 500 units from Flik, own Y, velocity zeroed) with vm_ip included in every sample this time, at finer 10-frame granularity. Hit connected at dist ~43307 (HP 6->4, flags->0x5043). Watched the FULL cycle end to end: ~30 frames outbound momentum (43307->49387 peak), then a clean ~130-frame accelerating approach (49387->10871, vx growing steadily to +1050 toward Flik), flag finally cleared at dist 10871 (0x5043->0x5041) with velocity reversing the same frame. vm_ip READ 0x800776A4 (the FIRST park_seek in the program, inside the first wander loop) at EVERY SINGLE SAMPLE across the entire cycle -- it never advanced to 0x800776FE (the program's own chase_radius_scratch) at any point.
AUDIT_2026-08-02_vm_ip_never_advances_du.conclusion: This is reassuring, not undermining: the observed chase movement is NOT the program's own scripted behavior at some opcode I happened not to be watching (e.g. an anchor/park-return coincidence) -- it structurally CANNOT be, since the program's IP never left its very first wander-loop instruction throughout an entire confirmed chase-and-disengage cycle. The movement is coming from the separate, already-documented global motion-phase override (vm_motion_apply_chase), which explicitly targets 'Flik's live position' per SYS_enemy_ai.md -- independent confirmation, at the architecture level, that this is genuine player-chase and not wander coincidentally read as chase. This is the fourth independent hit-trial to show the pattern (after trials 1 and 3 in the prior session), all consistent.
AUDIT_2026-08-02_vm_ip_never_advances_du.residual_not_closed_by_this: Still did not read vm_motion_apply_chase (0x8004C8AC) itself, so 'the override function is what's doing it' is inference from the existing Canon description plus vm_ip staying constant, not a direct instruction-level trace of that function executing (execTrace was not armed -- this fixture's movie predates the Interpreter-safety discovery and was handled poll-only throughout, consistent with every other session on this row).

STATIC_AUDIT_2026-08-02_who_sets_bit_0x2.gate_conditions: Three conditions must hold to reach the ori: (1) reading enemy_hp_table[actor_id*5 + equip_index] (0x80089938-based, the already-documented legacy HP side-table) yields < 0x78 (120); (2) the actor's own runtime-record backlink (+0x80(s2), dereferenced) has byte +0x11 == 0x64 (100); (3) the actor's own id (+0x00(s2), reloaded fresh at 0x800590E8) is NOT 13 and NOT 15. Redbug is id 19, so none of these exclusions apply to it -- consistent with observing the bit set reliably.
STATIC_AUDIT_2026-08-02_who_sets_bit_0x2.id_13_15_exclusion_interpretation_not_fu: id 15 = grasshopper (per Enemy_spawn_architecture.md's id table), which Enemy_AI_movement_programs.md separately categorizes as 'Native-assisted... chases via the global gate while parked' -- i.e. a DIFFERENT setter (a native CALL sub) rather than this hit-triggered path, which would explain why it's excluded here rather than contradicting its documented chase behavior. id 13's species was not identified (not in the 12-name list already on record) -- not chased further, tangential to D09.

RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.trigger: Enemy_death_and_permanence.md's own named residual (archived, predates this session): 'Directly observe a temporarily-KO'd enemy respawning to nail the temporary/permanent contrast end-to-end.' RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.scope: Fifth isolated instance, port 23499, config /tmp/duckstation-debugger-d09-respawn, stopped via the launcher at the end. Same fixture, load_start_state:true confirmed, advanced to frame 583 (HP 2, matching known state), then a manual berry throw to complete the kill (HP -> 0, same two-stage sequence as before).
RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.method: After confirming death (id=19, hp=0), watched continuously in 200-frame steps out to 4000 total frames (~66 seconds at 60Hz) post-death, reading the actor record (id/hp) and the live-enemy pointer table every step.
RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.result: hp stayed EXACTLY 0 at every single sample (200 through 4000 frames) -- no revival. The live-pointer-table slot the Redbug used to occupy stayed pointed at a different, unrelated actor throughout (never reclaimed by the Redbug).
RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.conclusion: NEGATIVE, and reasonably confident given the observation window: a temporarily-KO'd Redbug does NOT respawn within the same level session, at least not within 66 seconds. This is consistent with the already-documented actor-record architecture (Enemy_spawn_architecture.md / config/record_types.yaml: 'records are not reallocated during play' / reset only 'the next world-ready load overwrites the table') -- the negative result confirms that architecture applies to the temporary-KO case specifically, which had not been directly tested before. The archived note's 'quota still owes it -> may respawn' phrasing was speculative, not previously confirmed either way; this closes it for Redbug with a clean no.
RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_negative_result.not_tested: Whether leaving the level and RE-ENTERING (a full scene reload, not just waiting) brings it back -- not tested live here because the existing architecture (chunk-31 rebuild on load) already makes that outcome close to tautological (a level reload rebuilds every actor record fresh, dead or not), so a live test would mostly re-confirm already-established loader behavior rather than answer a new question. Named as the boundary of what this test covers, not silently assumed.

RESPAWN_TEST_2026-08-02_RETRACTED.retraction: ⚠️ RETRACTED 2026-08-02, same day as the original claim. Operator corrected this with direct gameplay knowledge (enemies come back only after the player leaves and returns, not while standing nearby), then guided a live re-test: killed a fresh Redbug, walked Flik away with REAL controller input (not a position poke) far enough (~76,000+ units, matching the same successful setup used for worm/D12), and watched -- hp reset to 6 (full), id stayed 19.
